raw_response:
I will still do it mostly the way I did before, because this land feeds my family and I do not gamble with it. I have 22.5 mu, and the main money still comes from wheat and maize, so I will keep the best ground in wheat-maize. Last year’s way is my base, then I shift a little by crop and by cost. If I put too little fertilizer and the crop turns thin, I lose more than the price of one extra bag, so on the grain land I will not be stingy. I have well water, so I will use it where it pays back, mainly on wheat, maize, cotton, and peanut. For the small crops, I will keep the area smaller because my family labor is limited and some people work outside. I will plant cotton and peanut on the lighter ground, millet and mung bean on the poorer or more troublesome patches, and I will do about what the better growers around me do when I see it works in their fields. Wheat will get the steadiest management, maize will follow the wheat stubble with less tillage to save labor, cotton will get more pesticide because insects can ruin it fast, and mung bean will get the lightest fertilizer because if I pour money into it, I do not always get it back.
